background.fact: DV is a family of digital video encodings developed for videocassettes in the early 1990s.
Its original specification came from a ten-company consortium and was standardized by IEC.
DV compresses pictures independently using a discrete cosine transform.
DVCAM and DVCPRO are related professional developments from Sony and Panasonic.
Raw DV-DIF files commonly use .dv or .dif; the same data can be wrapped in AVI, QuickTime or MXF.
DV-DIF divides the stream into 80-byte blocks carrying video, audio and auxiliary information.

windows.note: Free command-line tools; the official capability list includes DV demuxing and decoding.
Free player with a raw-DV demuxer explicitly registered for .dv; installed decoder support still determines which DV variants play.

mac.note: Free command-line tools; the official capability list includes DV demuxing and decoding.
Free player with a raw-DV demuxer explicitly registered for .dv; installed decoder support still determines which DV variants play.

linux.note: Free command-line tools; the official capability list includes DV demuxing and decoding.
Free player with a raw-DV demuxer explicitly registered for .dv; installed decoder support still determines which DV variants play.

problems.fact: The extension alone does not distinguish raw DV-DIF from DV data inside another wrapper; inspect the stream and container.
DV can include metadata attached to recorded frames; preservation work should inspect more than the visible picture.
A reader must support the specific DV variant; DVCPRO HD is not the same encoding profile as consumer DV.

background.fact: Khronos Texture version 1 is a texture container for OpenGL and OpenGL ES.
A KTX file stores texture dimensions and the GL format needed by its loader.
It can hold cubemap faces and texture arrays.
Mipmap levels are stored from largest to smallest.
A file may include named metadata values such as texture orientation.

windows.note: Free developer library that reads KTX version 1 and version 2; it is not a general photo viewer.
Free reader for KTX 1.0 files using ASTC texture formats; other KTX encodings are not accepted by this demuxer.
Free command-line utility for inspecting and decoding supported KTX/KTX2 texture payloads; available for Windows and Linux x64 and macOS arm64.
Texture-processing GUI and CLI available for Windows and Linux; its documented input list includes KTX and KTX2. Check the payload and chosen output settings.

mac.note: Free developer library that reads KTX version 1 and version 2; it is not a general photo viewer.
Free reader for KTX 1.0 files using ASTC texture formats; other KTX encodings are not accepted by this demuxer.
Free kramv viewer for supported KTX/KTX2 textures on Apple Silicon Macs; exposes mip levels, faces and array entries. Its README notes disabled Intel viewer support.

linux.note: Free developer library that reads KTX version 1 and version 2; it is not a general photo viewer.
Free reader for KTX 1.0 files using ASTC texture formats; other KTX encodings are not accepted by this demuxer.
Free command-line utility for inspecting and decoding supported KTX/KTX2 texture payloads; available for Windows and Linux x64 and macOS arm64.
Texture-processing GUI and CLI available for Windows and Linux; its documented input list includes KTX and KTX2. Check the payload and chosen output settings.

problems.fact: A texture may look upside down when its coordinate origin differs from the viewer; inspect KTXorientation.
A KTX texture does not guarantee that every OpenGL implementation supports its internal image format.
KTX2 has an incompatible container structure; changing its suffix to .ktx does not convert it.

background.fact: The .m2v suffix identifies an MPEG-2 video elementary stream.
MPEG-2 video is also known as ITU-T H.262 / MPEG-2 Part 2.
An elementary video stream contains picture content without an audio channel.
A program stream combines a single video content channel with associated audio.
A transport stream may multiplex several content channels and their audio.

windows.note: Free tools with MPEG-2 video decoding; FFmpeg documents .m2v for its raw MPEG-2 video output.
Free player whose MPEG-I/II elementary-video demuxer reads the kind of video stream carried by M2V; this supplies no missing audio track.
Switch 2.0 documents M2V elementary-stream input on Windows and Mac.

mac.note: Free tools with MPEG-2 video decoding; FFmpeg documents .m2v for its raw MPEG-2 video output.
Free player whose MPEG-I/II elementary-video demuxer reads the kind of video stream carried by M2V; this supplies no missing audio track.
Switch 2.0 documents M2V elementary-stream input on Windows and Mac.

linux.note: Free tools with MPEG-2 video decoding; FFmpeg documents .m2v for its raw MPEG-2 video output.
Free player whose MPEG-I/II elementary-video demuxer reads the kind of video stream carried by M2V; this supplies no missing audio track.

problems.fact: Silence is expected from a video-only elementary stream; an accompanying audio file must be supplied separately.
A program stream or transport stream is structurally different from an elementary stream; select the correct output stream type.
FFmpeg raw muxers accept only one stream and cannot store timestamps or metadata; use a suitable container when those are needed.

background.fact: MAC can identify an image in the legacy MacPaint format.
MacPaint pictures are black and white with a 576 by 720 pixel canvas.
The MacPaint data fork alone does not carry all the classic Mac file identification information.
MacPaint normally compresses its image data with run-length encoding.
A generated MacPaint image without that compression can still conform to the format.

windows.note: Free extractor whose supported raster formats include MacPaint.
Free command-line reader that writes the picture as PBM.

mac.note: Free extractor whose supported raster formats include MacPaint.
Free command-line reader that writes the picture as PBM.
The vendor manual lists MacPaint import and export for its monochrome image format.

linux.note: Free extractor whose supported raster formats include MacPaint.
Free command-line reader that writes the picture as PBM.

problems.fact: A shifted decoded picture can indicate an extra 128-byte Finder-information prefix introduced during transfer; macptopbm offers -extraskip.
A data-fork-only file may not identify as PNTG on classic Mac OS without a suitable MacBinary or BinHex wrapper.
The fixed MacPaint canvas cannot retain an arbitrarily large picture; the documented writer crops oversized input.

background.fact: Apple Motion lists .cdda among the audio file formats it can import.
Motion uses imported audio for music, dialogue and sound effects in a project.
Apple's archived iOS web-content reference groups .cdda with AIFF audio and the audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff media types.
AVFoundation identifies .cdda as an extension for AIFC audio under the public.aifc-audio uniform type identifier.
On macOS, the CDDAFS file system exposes tracks from a mounted audio CD as AIFF-C files.

mac.note: Imports .cdda audio into a motion-graphics project.

problems.fact: The suffix alone cannot verify the audio representation inside a particular .cdda file; inspect the actual file rather than assuming its encoding.
Motion resamples imported audio to the sample rate and bit depth used by the audio interface; project playback is not proof that those source properties remained unchanged.
For a .cdda file containing compressed AIFC audio, reading the container is only part of conversion: a decoder for the sound encoding must also be available.

background.fact: PCD is Kodak's Photo CD image format.
A standard Photo CD places numbered .pcd images in photo_cd/images.
The overview.pcd file supplies thumbnail images for a contact sheet.
Photo CD defines image sizes from 128 by 192 through 2048 by 3072 pixels.
ProPhotoCD adds a 4096 by 6144 pixel resolution.
The image representation stores luminance at full resolution and chromaticity at half resolution.

windows.note: Free for noncommercial use; reads PCD. Its Photo-CD plug-in adds high-resolution decoding.
Free command-line reader and writer for Photo CD; its documented write limit is 768 by 512 pixels.

mac.note: Free command-line reader and writer for Photo CD; its documented write limit is 768 by 512 pixels.
Photo CD decoder documented by Netpbm; distributed separately under restrictive licensing, rather than included in most installations.

linux.note: Free command-line reader and writer for Photo CD; its documented write limit is 768 by 512 pixels.
Photo CD decoder documented by Netpbm; distributed separately under restrictive licensing, rather than included in most installations.

problems.fact: A thumbnail extracted from overview.pcd is only Base/16 resolution; use the corresponding image file for a larger picture.
The highest ProPhotoCD resolution needs its extension files and original directory layout, so copying only one PCD can lose access to it.
ImageMagick writes Photo CD only up to 768 by 512 pixels; writing a PCD is not a preservation copy of a larger scan.
GraphicConverter's Mac App Store edition does not import PhotoCD.

background.fact: CRW is a Canon camera RAW format built on CIFF.
CIFF means Camera Image File Format.
CRW is structurally different from TIFF-based CR2 and QuickTime-based CR3.
Its file header specifies byte order and points to a root directory.
CIFF records organize data in a hierarchy of directories.
Canon's EOS Digital Rebel records RAW images as CRW.

windows.note: Free command-line reader; CRW appears as read-only in its format table.
Free metadata tool that inspects CRW/CIFF structure and tags; it is not a rendered-photo editor.
The camera-support table lists older Canon models and their required Camera Raw versions; check the exact model.

mac.note: Free command-line reader; CRW appears as read-only in its format table.
Free metadata tool that inspects CRW/CIFF structure and tags; it is not a rendered-photo editor.
Use the camera table to verify the particular Canon model and plug-in version.

linux.note: Free command-line reader; CRW appears as read-only in its format table.
Free metadata tool that inspects CRW/CIFF structure and tags; it is not a rendered-photo editor.

problems.fact: CRW, CR2 and CR3 use different structures; changing a suffix cannot translate between them.
Metadata and an embedded preview are not a substitute for decoding the RAW picture; inspect the record type before extracting data.
RAW support depends on the camera model and the library version actually bundled by the application.

background.fact: Digital Speech Standard is an audio format used in professional dictation.
DSS compresses recordings into compact files for dictation workflows.
The dictation workflow supports insert and overwrite recording.
DSS Classic recordings use .dss, while DSS Pro recordings use .ds2.
DSS Pro adds encryption and more index marks than classic DSS.

windows.note: Free decoder for DSS Standard Play; this does not establish support for DSS Pro/DS2.
The vendor provides a Windows dictation/transcription application.
The Dictation Module opens DSS and DSS Pro recordings in its playback window.

mac.note: Free decoder for DSS Standard Play; this does not establish support for DSS Pro/DS2.
The vendor manual documents DSS and DSS Pro playback.

linux.note: Free decoder for DSS Standard Play; this does not establish support for DSS Pro/DS2.

problems.fact: DSS and DS2 are related speech formats, but classic DSS does not have all the capabilities described for DSS Pro.
DSS Classic and DSS Pro are different; DSS Pro uses .ds2 rather than .dss.
FFmpeg's capability list names only DSS Standard Play decoding, so it cannot establish blanket support for every recorder mode.

background.fact: KTX2 is Khronos's second-generation GPU texture container.
It stores image data for graphics APIs such as Vulkan and OpenGL.
KTX2 supports texture arrays, cube maps and mipmap levels.
The registered media type is image/ktx2.
The container can hold supercompressed or universal texture data.
Its layout is incompatible with the original image/ktx container.

Free developer library that reads KTX version 1 and version 2; it is not a general photo viewer.

Texture-processing GUI and CLI available for Windows and Linux; its documented input list includes KTX and KTX2. Check the payload and chosen output settings.

web.note: The specification lists a Three.js loader for KTX2 assets; this is developer integration, not native browser image display.

problems.fact: A KTX1-only loader cannot read a KTX2 file just because the filename is renamed.
A universal compressed texture must be transcoded to a format supported by the destination GPU.
Mipmaps, array layers and cube faces are separate images; exporting a single image does not preserve the whole texture structure.
